76	## Scenarios
77	
78	| ID | Fault | What the checks see | Expected ending |
79	|---|---|---|---|
80	| DS-01 | A transformation change stops subtracting completed refunds | ETL green; net revenue overstated by exactly the succeeded refunds | Repair |
81	| DS-02 | A source migration renames `orders.total_amount` | ETL fails; analytics goes stale | Repair |
82	| DS-03 | The order fact is built with an inner join to payments | ETL green; orders with no payment are missing | Repair |
83	| DS-04 | The load becomes append-only, then a retry rereads a loaded batch | The deploy run is clean; the retry duplicates business keys and inflates revenue | Repair |
84	| DS-06 | The source starts writing refunds with a new status, `CHARGEBACK` | ETL green with rejected rows; those refunds are missing; revenue still reconciles | Escalation |
85	| DS-07 | Reporting days are assigned in UTC instead of the business timezone | ETL green; currency totals reconcile, individual days do not | Repair |
86	| DS-09 | `orders.total_amount` becomes nullable and some paid orders lose their amount | ETL green with rejected rows; those orders and their payments are missing | Escalation |
87	| DS-16 | Every refund subtracts the whole order amount | ETL green; net revenue understated, only on partial refunds | Repair |
88	| DS-17 | Failed payments count as revenue | ETL green; revenue overstated by exactly the failed payments | Repair |
89	
90	IDs follow the scenario table in the product brief; DS-16 and DS-17 are
91	additions to it. DS-04 takes two pipeline runs to show, which the lab performs
92	and reports. DS-06 and DS-09 have no correct transformation change: the
93	workflow is expected to say so and hand the incident to a person.
94	
95	Each scenario carries a briefing for the lab's operator (what it changes,
96	what you will see, which checks should fail, how it should end) and an answer
97	key (`ground_truth`) that only the evaluator reads. Neither reaches an agent:
98	nothing an agent can call imports the scenario package (a test enforces
99	this), no prompt contains it, and an incident never names its scenario.
100	
101	## Safety model
102	
103	- **Agents only read.** The investigation tools connect with a PostgreSQL role
104	  that can `SELECT` from the source, the analytics target, and the
105	  transformation history, and nothing else. No tool accepts SQL; queries are
106	  templates with typed parameters.
107	- **Codex has no shell.** Each turn runs with the shell and web search
108	  disabled and a read-only sandbox, so the MCP tools are its only reach.
109	- **Evidence comes from tool results.** The adapter reads the tool calls from
110	  Codex's event stream and fails a turn unless the role's required calls
111	  succeeded. The model's description of a result is never stored as evidence.
112	- **A repair is data, not code.** It is a new version of one allowlisted file,
113	  `etl/transforms/order_revenue.yaml`, and is accepted only if it parses
114	  against a strict schema and changes a handful of lines.
115	- **Deterministic checks decide.** Staging validation, approval checks, and
116	  post-fix verification are code. A model's statement that something passed
117	  proves nothing.
118	- **A repair must survive a retry.** Staging loads the same rows a second
119	  time and reruns every check, so a patch that leaves the load non-idempotent
120	  is rejected even though a fresh staging load of it looks clean.
121	- **Approval is bound to the patch.** The executor re-reads the proposal, the
122	  approval, and the validation result and refuses unless all three name the
123	  same hash and the patch still applies to the deployed version.
124	- **Prompts are fixed templates.** No text typed into the web application
125	  reaches a prompt. Mutating routes can require a demo access code, and
126	  investigations are capped per hour and per day.
127	- **Unclear business rules go to a human.** A missing contract, or a rule the
128	  analyst cannot find, escalates the incident instead of being assumed.
129	
130	## Tests and evaluation
131	
132	```sh
133	.venv/bin/python -m pytest                           # 130 tests, about a minute and a half
134	.venv/bin/python -m datatracemind.evaluation DS-01   # one real run, scored
135	```
136	
137	The tests use a separate `datatracemind_test` database and spend no model
138	usage: the workflow is driven by a scripted stand-in provider whose tool calls
139	are real. They cover every scenario from injection to its expected ending,
140	and the blocked paths as well as the happy one: applying without approval, a
141	changed patch after approval, a patch that failed validation, rejection, and
142	a failed post-fix verification.
143	
144	The evaluator resets the demo, injects a scenario, runs a real investigation,
145	and scores it against the answer key. Results are written to
146	`evaluation/results/`.
147

149	
150	```
151	contracts/        approved business definitions (revenue, orders, source schema)
152	etl/              pipeline, transformation, quality checks, run log
153	simulator/        seeded transaction generator
154	infra/postgres/   schema for source, analytics target, and application state
155	datatracemind/
156	  api/            FastAPI routes
157	  monitoring/     detection and dashboard read models
158	  scenarios/      fault scenarios, their briefings, and their answer keys
159	  tools/          read-only investigation tools and the MCP server
160	  llm/            provider contract and the Codex adapter
161	  agents/         role prompts and the role runner

163	  repair/         proposals, staging validation, approval, executor
164	  observability/  neatlogs tracing

166	frontend/         React: the incident console (/) and the Scenario Lab (/lab/)

168	```
169	
170	## Hackathon tools
171	
172	- **neatlogs** traces every investigation: one trace per run, a span per role,
173	  per Codex turn (with token usage and estimated cost), and per tool call.
174	  Approval, apply, and verification are traced as guardrail spans in the same
175	  session.
176	- **Entire** captures the coding-agent sessions behind each commit.
177	- **cfo.ai** holds the business plan; the measured cost per investigation
178	  feeds it.
179	
180	## Deviations from the plan
181	
182	- The simulator is Python, not Spring Boot. The `oltp` schema is its only
183	  interface to the pipeline, so another producer can replace it.
184	- The analytics target is a PostgreSQL schema, the plan's documented fallback
185	  to ClickHouse.
186	- The ETL worker runs as a thread inside the API process rather than as its
187	  own service.
188	- Contract lookup runs before the two investigators rather than beside them,
189	  so a missing definition escalates before any model usage is spent.
190	- Two database credentials exist (application and read-only), not a third
191	  repair-only one. The executor's single write is deploying a new version of
192	  the transformation file.
193	
194	## Known limitations
195	
196	- Only DS-01 has been run with the real model so far: three investigations,
197	  one of them taken through approval, apply, and verification. Every other
198	  scenario passes end to end with the scripted provider only, so how the real
199	  model diagnoses DS-02 through DS-17, and whether it escalates DS-06 and
200	  DS-09 as intended, is not yet known.
201	- With DS-04 active and live traffic running, the duplication keeps growing:
202	  each run rereads the last few seconds and appends them again. That is the
203	  fault behaving as it would in production, not a second fault.
204	- Cost figures are estimates at API list prices; the model runs on a
205	  flat-rate ChatGPT plan.
206	- There is no container image for the API yet, and the stack has not been
207	  deployed.

220	# creative-engine
221	
222	Creative-engine contains a local controls service, dependency-free contract validators, and a typed non-UI creative API runtime. The controls package validates bounded creative changes and stores a durable local Apply outbox. The API handler implements generate/edit/inspect/list/compare/restore/cancel/handoff and job status around injected jobs, storage, provider, DecisionPort, metering, approval, inspection, handoff, and telemetry ports. Current generate/edit/inspection/DecisionPort attempts require explicit usage profiles and persist sanitized attempt evidence on the same SQLite connection as the durable API store. Its public contract and C01/C02/C03/C04 schemas remain local proposals pending external owner agreement; production provider transports, application authentication, finance authority, approval issuance, and rendering are not implemented here.
223	
224	The `creative-engine/versions` subpath exposes a local SQLite-backed version adapter that pairs immutable design records and exact content-addressed artifact bytes with selection CAS and API job completion in one database transaction. Recovery and restore do not dispatch providers. Handoff remains unavailable until durable external-result staging is implemented. Local tests do not certify production-host durability or external acceptance.
225	
226	The `creative-engine/telemetry` subpath exposes the CE-11 usage/evidence boundary and SQLite outbox. It reuses the C03 metering authority and does not create a budget ledger. The local outbox refuses to append or claim externally deliverable records inside an uncommitted outer transaction. Neatlogs protocol agreement, actual ingestion, and readback remain unresolved; passing local checks does not satisfy those gates.
227	
228	## Build and offline checks
229	
230	Use Node.js 22.23.3 for the production-target checks. Node.js 24.15.0 is also checked for development compatibility. From the repository root:
231	
232	```sh
233	make bootstrap
234	make build
235	make check TARGET=api MODE=mock
236	make check TARGET=controls MODE=mock
237	make check TARGET=contracts MODE=mock
238	make check TARGET=decision-contract MODE=mock
239	make check TARGET=eval-policy MODE=mock
240	make check TARGET=metering-contract MODE=mock
241	make check TARGET=handoff-contract MODE=mock
242	make check TARGET=access-preflight MODE=mock
243	make check TARGET=access-preflight MODE=live
244	make check TARGET=versions MODE=mock
245	make check TARGET=creative-metering MODE=mock
246	make check TARGET=all MODE=mock
247	```
248	
249	The API, contract, control, evaluation-policy, access-preflight, and versions checks use synthetic fixtures and make no paid provider calls. `make check TARGET=api MODE=mock` writes a sanitized, versioned summary to `build/api-check-evidence.json`. `make check TARGET=access-preflight MODE=mock` exercises the fixed eight-cell access matrix, writes sanitized mock evidence to `build/access-preflight-evidence.json`, and keeps acceptance pending. `make check TARGET=access-preflight MODE=live` writes `build/access-preflight-live-gate.json`, prints the blocked per-cell reasons, and exits 2 with zero provider dispatches when trusted live adapters and external owner evidence are absent. A user-supplied JSON claim cannot enable live access. The exported `runAccessPreflight` API can be composed by a trusted host with real owner adapters; this repository does not install that host or read credentials. `make acceptance TARGET=access-preflight` reports the same missing live owner evidence and exits 2. `make check TARGET=versions MODE=mock` runs the paired durable API/store and process-restart cases, plus strict public-subpath typechecking. `make check TARGET=eval-policy MODE=mock` runs the policy, corpus, register, report, and acceptance-gate fixtures; local checks may pass while owner evidence remains pending. `make acceptance TARGET=api`, `make acceptance TARGET=contracts`, `make acceptance TARGET=decision-contract`, `make acceptance TARGET=metering-contract`, `make acceptance TARGET=handoff-contract`, and `make acceptance TARGET=versions` intentionally fail while canonical owner agreements remain pending. `make acceptance TARGET=eval-policy` separately emits machine-readable evidence and exits 2 until accountable owners publish and independently verify the required corpus, question inventory, rubric, telemetry, budget, and policy approvals. `make acceptance TARGET=all` includes those agreements, CE-Q01 policy/corpus evidence, and the CE-A01 live access gate.
250	
251	The standalone workflows check the public API, contract, metering, approval-handoff, preflight, versions, and telemetry package imports with TypeScript 5.9.3 in strict NodeNext mode. `make bootstrap` installs the locked TypeScript consumer tools used by those checks. Run `make typecheck-api`, `make typecheck-preflight`, `make typecheck-versions`, or `make typecheck-telemetry` to check the public consumers directly. The supported runtime checks use Node.js 22.23.3 and Node.js 24.15.0.
252	
253	`make check TARGET=creative-metering MODE=mock` exercises the current generate, edit, inspection, and DecisionPort attempt paths against injected fixture ports. It checks usage profiles, durable outbox identity, replay, and rejection before reservation when evidence cannot be committed. Planning and repair remain required future local integrations. Responses orchestration is optional until selected; any selected billable path must use C03 metering and this evidence boundary. `make acceptance TARGET=creative-metering` exits 2 because no authoritative Neatlogs evidence-sink agreement reference or verified ingestion/readback is available; the Finance and usage-schema agreement checks do not override this gate.
254	
255	```sh
256	make typecheck-api
257	make typecheck-contracts
258	```
259	
260	The controls browser example has its own lockfile and dependency install. Its Node and Chromium roundtrip instructions, local evidence format, and remaining integration requirements are in [controls integration](docs/controls-integration.md). It uses mock application identity and state.

287	# Mekiki
288	
289	Mekiki (目利き) means a trained eye for quality. It's a small AI agent that recommends npm packages. Ask it which library to use, and it looks up real registry data before answering with one pick and up to two alternatives.
290	
291	It's a practice project, built to learn how agents work before [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon). The whole agent fits in one file of about 250 lines: a tool calling loop, two tools, and tracing with [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com).
292	
293	```
294	$ npm start -- "best React form library?"
295	
296	[step 1] get_package_info({"name": "formik"})
297	[step 1] get_package_info({"name": "react-hook-form"})
298	[step 1] get_package_info({"name": "redux-form"})
299	[step 1] get_package_info({"name": "@tanstack/react-form"})
300	[step 1] search_packages({"query": "react form library"})
301	
302	### Recommendation:
303	**Primary:** **React Hook Form** ...
304	**Alternatives:**
305	- **Formik** ...
306	- **@tanstack/react-form** ...
307	
308	(answer shortened; the real one lists downloads and publish dates for each)
309	```
310	
311	## What you need
312	
313	- **Node 22 or later.** The `openai` package needs it. Check with `node -v`.
314	- **An OpenAI API key** from [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys). A run costs about $0.0006 with `gpt-4o-mini`, so a hundred runs cost less than ten cents.
315	- **A neatlogs account**, free at [app.neatlogs.com](https://app.neatlogs.com). This is where you'll see what the agent did on each run.
316	
317	## Setup
318	
319	1. Clone the repo and install:
320	
321	   ```bash
322	   git clone https://github.com/atharvdange618/Mekiki.git
323	   cd Mekiki
324	   npm install
325	   ```
326	
327	2. Copy the example env file:
328	
329	   ```bash
330	   cp .env.example .env
331	   ```
332	
333	3. Fill in `.env`:
334	
335	   | Variable           | Where to get it                                                                                                |
336	   | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
337	   | `OPENAI_API_KEY`   | OpenAI dashboard, API keys                                                                                     |
338	   | `OPENAI_MODEL`     | Any chat model on your account. We used `gpt-4o-mini`, which is cheap and fails often enough to be interesting |
339	   | `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | neatlogs dashboard, **Settings → API Keys**                                                                    |
340	
341	   `.env` is in `.gitignore`. Never commit it, and never paste keys into chat.
342	
343	4. Check that everything typechecks:
344	
345	   ```bash
346	   npm run typecheck
347	   ```
348	
349	## Run it
350	
351	```bash
352	npm start
353	npm start -- "which HTTP client should I use in Node?"
354	```
355	
356	With no question, it asks about date libraries. Each run prints the tool calls it makes as `[step N]` lines, then the answer. The last line, `[neatlogs] Neatlogs SDK shutdown complete`, means the trace was sent.
357	
358	This works the same in Git Bash on Windows, macOS and Linux.
359	
360	## See the trace
361	
362	Open [app.neatlogs.com](https://app.neatlogs.com) and find the newest trace in the `npm-advisor` workflow. Each run is one trace:
363	
364	```
365	WORKFLOW advise
366	└─ AGENT npm_advisor
367	   ├─ LLM            one per model turn, with tokens and cost
368	   ├─ TOOL search_packages
369	   └─ TOOL get_package_info
370	```
371	
372	Click any `TOOL` span to see exactly what data the model got. Most of what we learned building this came from reading those spans, not the final answer.
373	
374	## How it works
375	
376	The agent is a loop. It sends the conversation and two tool descriptions to the model. If the model asks for tools, the loop runs them in parallel, adds the results to the conversation, and asks again. When the model answers without asking for a tool, that's the final answer.
377	
378	| Tool               | What it does                                                                                                     |
379	| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
380	| `search_packages`  | Searches npm, returns the 8 most downloaded of 25 matches                                                        |
381	| `get_package_info` | Looks up one package: version, last publish date, months since then, license, repository, downloads, deprecation |
382	
383	The system prompt tells the model to name the packages it already knows for the job, check them with `get_package_info`, and search for anything it missed. Its memory knows what developers choose. The tools know what's current.
384	
385	[`architecture.md`](architecture.md) has the full picture.
386	
387	## Things to try
388	
389	Each of these teaches something we ran into for real.
390	
391	1. **Read a trace end to end.** Run the form question and open its trace. Find the moment the model chose its alternatives, and look at what the tool spans handed it.
392	2. **Run the same question five times.** The answers change. One run proves nothing, which is why every fix here was measured over several.
393	3. **Score the holdout questions.** [`evals.md`](evals.md) has three questions with answer keys written before any run. Run them, score them, and compare with our results.
394	4. **Take on the open problem.** The last fix made main picks perfect but broke the alternatives. [`decisions.md`](decisions.md) explains the three causes. Try a prompt change, then measure it on questions you didn't tune on.
395	5. **Break it.** If npm returns an error, the agent crashes instead of telling the model. Turn off your network mid-run and find the crash in neatlogs. Then make the tool return the error to the model and see whether it recovers.
396	6. **Swap the model.** Change `OPENAI_MODEL` and rerun the holdout. Does a bigger model still trust a 2023 package?
397	
398	## Agent sessions with Entire
399	
400	We write much of this repo with AI coding agents, so the reasoning behind a change often lives in a chat that no one else sees. [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) saves that chat. When you commit, it records the agent session behind the commit (your prompts, the agent's replies, the files it touched) as a checkpoint and links it to that commit.
401	
402	Here's why that matters for this project. `decisions.md` tells you what we changed and why, in our own words. A checkpoint shows the session where it happened, so when someone asks why a prompt line exists, you can read the conversation that produced it instead of guessing.
403	
404	Checkpoints live in git refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/`, apart from your branches, so they never show up in `git log` or in a PR diff. Entire pushes them to `origin` along with your normal pushes.
405	
406	### What's in the repo
407	
408	| File                          | What it does                                                                                                   |
409	| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
410	| `.entire/settings.json`       | Turns Entire on for this repo and stores checkpoints as git refs                                                |
411	| `.entire/.gitignore`          | Keeps local logs, temp files and per machine settings out of git                                                |
412	| `.claude/settings.json`       | Claude Code hooks. They tell Entire when a session starts and ends, when you send a prompt, and when the agent stops |
413	| `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | The same hooks for OpenCode. `entire enable --agent opencode` generates it, so don't edit it by hand            |
414	| `.agents/hooks.json`          | The same hooks for Antigravity                                                                                  |
415	
416	Each hook checks for the `entire` command first and exits quietly if it can't find it. If you don't install Entire, your agents work as before and nothing gets recorded. Claude Code will print a one line note at session start with a link to the install guide.
417	
418	### Setup
419	
420	1. Install the CLI with the [install guide](https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation#installation-methods).
421	2. From the repo root, run:
422	
423	   ```bash
424	   entire enable
425	   ```
426	
427	   The agent hooks are already committed, but the git hooks that link sessions to commits live in `.git/hooks`, which git never shares. This step installs them on your machine.
428	
429	3. Check that it worked:
430	
431	   ```bash
432	   entire status
433	   ```
434	
435	   You should see `Enabled`, the three agents (Antigravity, Claude Code, OpenCode), and `Checkpoints sync to: origin`.
436	
437	### Using it
438	
439	| Command                          | What it does                                    |
440	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
441	| `entire status`                  | Shows whether Entire is on and any live sessions |
442	| `entire checkpoint list`         | Lists checkpoints on the current branch          |
443	| `entire checkpoint explain <sha>` | Shows the session behind a commit               |
444	| `entire search "query"`          | Searches checkpoints, commits and sessions       |
445	
446	## Project docs
447	
448	| File                                 | What's in it                                                                         |
449	| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
450	| [`architecture.md`](architecture.md) | How the agent works, its tools, tracing, and known gaps                              |
451	| [`decisions.md`](decisions.md)       | Every change, why we made it, what we rejected, and the numbers before and after     |
452	| [`evals.md`](evals.md)               | Test questions, answer keys, scored results, and predictions written before each run |
453	
454	## Scripts
455	
456	| Command             | What it does                                                   |
457	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
458	| `npm start`         | Runs the agent. Add `-- "your question"` to ask something else |
459	| `npm run typecheck` | Runs `tsc --noEmit`                                            |

=================== PRADDZY__jobsmith README
# JobSmith

**Would you hire an AI for this support role?**

JobSmith starts from a public support job listing, identifies one repeatable task with a quote from the listing, builds a bounded AI workflow for that task, and puts it through practice and unseen synthetic cases. It ends with a clear recommendation for a **supervised sandbox pilot** or **no-go**.

No customer inbox is connected. JobSmith never sends a reply, changes an account, or uses real customer records.

## The user flow

1. Discover support openings through CrustData, or choose a clearly labeled bundled sample if CrustData is unavailable.
2. Select one role. Qwen extracts a repeatable duty and must cite an exact line from the listing.
3. Qwen designs a narrow workflow that may prepare unsent drafts or recommend human review. It cannot take account actions.
4. Evaluate the workflow on role-family practice cases. The workflow may be revised at most twice using practice results.
5. Evaluate the final workflow on a separate held-out set. A live-model run on a live listing can become a supervised pilot candidate only if every held-out check passes. Sample runs always remain previews.
6. Review the evidence, safety boundaries, and an editable, assumption-labeled capacity estimate.

The synthetic suite has eight practice cases and eight held-out cases across billing, account access, security, and workspace membership. The workflow evaluates only the task family supported by the selected role duty. Passing synthetic checks is a small signal, not a production accuracy claim.

## What each platform does

| Platform | Job in JobSmith |
| --- | --- |
| CrustData | Finds public support-role listings and source links. |
| GMI Cloud | Runs `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Max` for role-duty extraction, workflow design, revisions, and ticket decisions. |
| Neatlogs | Captures the role-to-decision trace, including model and evaluation steps. |
| Entire | Records the code evolution in the Git workflow. It is not a runtime dependency. |
| cfo.ai | Holds the separate operating and customer-pilot planning scenarios. It is not connected to the app's runtime economics estimate. |

## Run locally

Requirements: Node.js 22+ and npm.

```powershell
npm ci
Copy-Item .env.example .env.local
# Add service keys locally. Never commit .env.local.
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). The app creates `data/jobsmith.sqlite` on first use. Without a GMI Cloud key, JobSmith uses deterministic sample rules; the result is visibly labeled **Sample preview** and cannot qualify as a pilot candidate. Without CrustData, the role cards are visibly labeled sample listings.

## Configuration

| Variable | Used for | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GMICLOUD_API_KEY` | Live role analysis and workflow evaluation | Missing key selects the labeled sample preview. |
| `GMICLOUD_BASE_URL` | GMI Cloud OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1` |
| `GMICLOUD_MODEL` | Model selection | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Max` |
| `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` | Live support-role discovery | Missing or unavailable API returns bundled sample listings with a warning. |
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | Trace export | Optional for local use. |
| `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` | Trace ingestion | `https://ingest.neatlogs.com` |
| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite filename under `data/` | `jobsmith.sqlite` |

The cfo.ai connection is managed separately through Codex MCP. It does not require credentials in the app environment.

## Demo script

1. Start by stating: “We help a SaaS founder decide whether a real support-role task is safe enough for a supervised AI pilot.”
2. Select a live CrustData role and point to the quoted duty evidence. If using sample data, say so before starting.
3. Start probation. Show role extraction, workflow design, practice evaluation, and up to two revisions.
4. Explain the boundary: the model can prepare an unsent draft or ask for a person; it cannot touch a customer system.
5. Open the final held-out checks. Explain the pass gate and the small synthetic sample limitation.
6. Show the editable capacity estimate as an assumption-based planning aid, not a forecast.
7. In the hackathon pitch, show Neatlogs trace evidence and Entire code evolution separately. Explain cfo.ai's separate planning use without suggesting the app is linked to it.

Keep the walkthrough under three minutes. Do not imply production readiness or use real customer data.

## Architecture

```text
Next.js role-to-pilot workspace
  ├─ /api/discovery                CrustData search or labeled sample fallback
  ├─ /api/pilots                   create and list persisted pilot runs
  ├─ /api/pilots/[id]              retrieve run state and evidence
  ├─ /api/pilots/[id]/resume       continue saved role-to-pilot state machine
  ├─ pilot-agent                   structured role extraction and workflow design
  ├─ support agent                 GMI Cloud structured decisions, no answer key
  ├─ scoring                       server-side synthetic practice/held-out checks
  ├─ SQLite                        additive pilot history; prior evaluation runs remain
  └─ neatlogs                      role, workflow, model, and evaluation traces
```

The model receives the customer question, the selected bounded workflow, and relevant synthetic policy articles. It does not receive evaluator answer labels, expected article IDs, fixture practice/holdout status, or synthetic customer identities. Scores and the final gate are computed server-side. Each completed case is saved so a failed run can resume without repeating finished work.

## Development checks

```powershell
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

The tests use synthetic data and do not require external keys.

## Submission and data boundaries

- Public code includes the Neatlogs, CrustData, and GMI Cloud application paths; no credentials are committed.
- `.env.local`, SQLite data, AWS setup notes, and Neatlogs setup notes are ignored by Git.
- Job listing text is public source material; all customer cases and policy articles are synthetic.
- cfo.ai plans and Entire activity are shown separately from the app runtime.
- No support inbox, customer database, reply delivery, or account-action integration exists.

=================== harsh-madhav__upshift README
# Upshift

Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass.

Upshift is an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. Give it a Python repo and a package to
upgrade, or let it find the vulnerable ones. It researches the upgrade itself (changelog, release notes, migration guide, and an API diff
made by installing both versions), writes a playbook where every rule cites its source, bumps the
dependency, fixes the code one root cause at a time, and proves nothing new broke against the test
baseline it recorded before touching anything.

Built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Bring your own model key.

## Status

Package bumps, vulnerability scans and Python version upgrades work end to end. Third-party API drift
comes next.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/overview) with
its graph plugin (`entire plugin install graph`). Without Entire the agent still runs, but its graph tools and the
`entire graph verify` check report that they are unavailable.

```bash
uv sync
python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --install   # pre-commit hook that blocks committed keys
cp .env.example .env                         # fill in your provider and key (git-ignored)

# no model calls: clone, baseline, research, bump, and show what breaks
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2 --dry-run

# the full agent
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2
uv run upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app                     # find known vulnerabilities and fix each one
uv run upshift python --repo demo/shop_app --to 3.12         # move to a newer Python and fix what breaks
uv run upshift resume <run-id>     # continue a crashed or killed run
```

Runs live in `.upshift/runs/<run-id>/`: the working copy, its venv, `state.json`, the research sources and
the report. Playbooks are cached in `playbooks/` and reused by the next repo on the same upgrade.

## Models: bring your own key

Set `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` and `UPSHIFT_MODEL` plus that provider's key in `.env` (read automatically,
never committed) or in your shell.

| `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` | Needs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` defaults to `claude-opus-5-5`. Claude's thinking blocks are replayed unchanged and old tool results are trimmed by the API's context editing, so the conversation stays append-only |
| `azure-openai` | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` is the deployment name |
| `litellm` | `LITELLM_API_KEY` | A LiteLLM proxy. Defaults to the [neatHack model proxy](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models) (Claude and Amazon Nova, e.g. `REDACTED.6`); set `LITELLM_BASE_URL` for your own |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for any OpenAI-compatible service (OpenRouter, Groq, Together, a local server) |
| `bedrock` | `UPSHIFT_AWS_PROFILE` | An explicit profile is required, so the default AWS account is never billed by accident |

The agent uses one message format internally and each provider translates to it, so adding a
provider means one adapter in `upshift/llm.py`. Every client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap`, so
model calls are traced with tokens and latency whichever provider you pick.

## How a job runs

| Phase | What happens | Where the tools come in |
|---|---|---|
| setup | Clone, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI | |
| baseline | Run the tests before changing anything | `entire graph verify --record-baseline` |
| bump | Rewrite the pins, install the new version, see what breaks | |
| research | Docs, changelog, GitHub release notes, API diff of both installed versions → cited playbook. Skipped for a security fix that breaks nothing | neatlogs `RETRIEVER`/`AGENT` spans |
| fix | One root cause per round. Progress is committed, regressions are reverted | `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools, one neatlogs span per round |
| verify | No new failures against the baseline, no old APIs left from the playbook; for security fixes, pip-audit again | `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` |
| report | `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with changes, verification and sources | |

Every job is one neatlogs trace.

`upshift scan` installs the repo once, audits the exact installed versions with
[pip-audit](https://github.com/pypa/pip-audit) (OSV advisories, transitive dependencies included) and starts
one job per vulnerable package, like one PR each. The target is the smallest release that fixes every advisory,
preferring the current major line. A fix that breaks nothing is just a pin change with no model calls; one that
breaks the code goes through research and the fix loop like any other upgrade.

`upshift python` moves the version pins (`.python-version`, Dockerfile base image, GitHub Actions, tox, and
`requires-python` / ruff / mypy targets in pyproject.toml), rebuilds the venv on the new Python and fixes what
breaks. Its research is the Removed, Porting and Deprecated sections of each What's New page in range, plus a diff
of the standard library under both interpreters. If a pinned dependency has no release for the new Python, the job
stops and names it, so it can be upgraded first with `upshift bump`.

## Tests

```bash
uv run pytest
```

The fix-loop tests drive the real loop (repo, venv, pytest, git) with a scripted model in place of a real one.

# RelayZero — the $0 agent that never goes down

**Team ArcOmega · neatHack 2026 entry**

> Every model is free. Every model will fail. The agent finishes anyway.

RelayZero is a single end-to-end agent that completes tasks on **$0 of inference**
by routing across a bench of **free model seats** with live failover. Give it a
goal, kill its model mid-run — it cools the seat down, restores state from an
[Entire](https://entire.io) checkpoint, fails over to the next free seat, verifies
its own answer, and finishes.

## The loop

```
plan → route → execute → verify
            ↑                |
            └─ failover ←----+  (checkpoint → cool seat → restore → retry)
```

Every run is traced end-to-end in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) (spans for
plan / route / llm-call / verify / recover, with latency, tokens, cost=$0.00).

## Quickstart

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env   # fill in your FREE seat keys (see below)
python3 relay.py "Research three free LLM observability tools and compare them"
```

Kill-test (the demo centerpiece):

```bash
RELAYZERO_KILL_SEAT=groq python3 relay.py "Write a haiku about failing over, then explain the poem"
```

## Free seats

| Seat | Provider | Endpoint | Free model (verified 2026-10-10) |
|------|----------|----------|----------------------------------|
| groq | Groq | api.groq.com/openai/v1 | qwen/qwen3.8-27b |
| openrouter | OpenRouter | openrouter.ai/api/v1 | nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free |
| gemini | Google AI | generativelanguage.googleapis.com | gemini-flash-latest |
| mistral | Mistral AI | api.mistral.ai/v1 | mistral-small-latest (rate-limited at bench time) |
| nous | Nous Research | inference-api.nousresearch.com | needs account-level user tag (bench skips) |
| nvidia | NVIDIA NIM | integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 | key not provisioned for chat models (bench skips) |

Dropped: SambaNova — free tier gates inference behind a payment method (fails the
no-billing rule). `bench()` probes every seat at startup — the agent only routes
to seats that actually answer. Seats are disposable by design.

## Kill test (verified 2026-10-10)

Full run log: [evidence/kill-test-2026-10-10.txt](evidence/kill-test-2026-10-10.txt)

```
$ RELAYZERO_KILL_SEAT=groq python relay.py "Write a haiku about failing over…"
  [!] groq failed (500); cooling down, failing over…
  [✓] answered by gemini (7115.3 ms, cost $0.00)
  verifier score: 10 (seat: openrouter)
  failovers: 1 | cost: $0.00
```

The agent did not restart — it restored state from the pre-call checkpoint,
failed over to the next live free seat, verified the answer with a second seat,
and delivered.

## Before/after: v1 naive → v2 backoff+verify

Full comparison: [evidence/before-after-v1-v2.txt](evidence/before-after-v1-v2.txt)

| metric | v1 naive (`--naive`) | v2 backoff+verify (default) |
|---|---|---|
| failed calls to the dead seat | 2 (immediate same-seat retry) | 1 (30s cooldown) |
| checkpoint restore on failover | no | yes |
| answer verifier | none | second seat, 10/10 |
| inference cost | $0.00 | $0.00 |

The neatlogs traces told the story: v1's recover spans showed back-to-back 500s
on the same seat — wasted calls with zero information gain. That's what
motivated the cooldown + checkpoint-restore design in v2.

## Sponsor evidence

- **neatlogs**: every run traced from commit #1 — spans for plan/route/llm-call/
  recover/verify with latency, tokens, cost. Live dashboard links pending the
  free no-card account (in progress); meanwhile every span also buffers to
  `local_traces/` JSONL. Trace the kill test: `RELAYZERO_KILL_SEAT=groq python
  relay.py "…"` and read the recover/failover spans.
- **Entire**: the agent wraps each run in Entire's session lifecycle
  (`entire_wrap.py`) and commits its own run artifacts — every agent commit is
  a replayable checkpoint. Evidence: `evidence/entire-checkpoint-explain.txt`
  (checkpoint `01M4JBMESRM5N1J1G16DR8KE6C`), per-run transcripts in
  `evidence/runs/<run_id>/transcript.jsonl`.
- **cfo.ai**: business numbers exported as CSV (`business/pricing-tiers.csv`,
  `business/scenarios.csv`, `business/unit-economics.csv`), ready for upload;
  Ari forecasts land day 2.

## The business (preview)

RelayZero as a $0-inference agent API: inference costs $0, gross margin on
inference is 100%, break-even ≈ 35 Pro customers. Full plan via cfo.ai (day 2).

# Fixpoint — the self-healing test agent

> Built for **neatHack 2026** (team **AI LONE STAR**). Theme: *build an agent you'd trust to run without you watching.*
> Repo: https://github.com/JMadhan1/fixpoint

Fixpoint takes a repository with a **failing test suite** and autonomously drives it to **all-green**: it reads the failures, locates the bug using a map of the codebase, fixes the source, re-runs the tests, and — crucially — **reverts its own change when a fix breaks another test**. Then it stops and explains what it did.

## Why this is interesting

Two things separate a demo you can trust from one you can't: **recovery from failure** and a **measurable improvement over time**. In Fixpoint both are the task itself, not an afterthought:

- **Recovery is real.** The demo repo contains a shared helper used by two functions. The *obvious* fix to one bug breaks the other. Fixpoint detects the regression, reverts, and fixes it locally instead. (We seeded this on purpose so the recovery is reproducible.)
- **Improvement is measured.** We run two versions of the agent and compare real, neatlogs-traced numbers:
  - **v1 baseline** — no codebase context, no recovery guard.
  - **v2 improved** — Entire-Graph repo map + a verify-and-revert loop.

## The three required tools form one story

```
neatlogs (observe)  ──►  Entire (improve)  ──►  neatlogs (prove)  ──►  cfo.ai (monetize)
```

1. **neatlogs** traces v1 and shows it thrashing — re-reading files, burning tokens, leaving regressions.
2. **Entire Graph** gives the agent a map of the codebase (Entire reports up to 71% token savings) and **Entire checkpoints** version each iteration.
3. **neatlogs** on v2 proves fewer steps, fewer tokens, lower cost, more tests fixed, zero regressions.
4. **cfo.ai** turns that halved token cost into the product's margin story — the engineering win *is* the business win.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `demo_app_broken/` | The target repo — `storekit` library with 7 planted bugs + pytest suite |
| `fixpoint/` | The agent: `agent.py` (loop), `workspace.py` (tools + test runner), `repo_map.py` (Entire-Graph context), `pricing.py` |
| `run.py` | Run one agent variant: `python run.py v1` / `python run.py v2` |
| `compare.py` | Build the before/after evidence table → `docs/BEFORE_AFTER.md` |
| `hackathon.md` | Dated, evidence-based build log (neatHack requirement) |
| `BUSINESS_PLAN.md` | cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) |
| `SUBMISSION.md` | Every rubric item mapped to its evidence |
| `docs/SETUP.md` | Step-by-step: keys, neatlogs, Entire on Windows, cfo.ai |
| `docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md` | Shot-by-shot 3-minute demo video script |
| `docs/BUILD_IN_PUBLIC.md` | Ready-to-post #neatHack updates |

## Quickstart

**See the whole flow now, with no API key and no cost** (a scripted brain drives the *real* harness — real pytest, real regression, real revert):

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python run.py v1 --simulate   # baseline: leaves regressions, fails
python run.py v2 --simulate   # improved: catches a regression, reverts, goes green
python compare.py             # -> docs/BEFORE_AFTER.md
python report.py              # -> docs/report.html  (open in a browser)
python -m pytest -q           # 5 offline harness tests
```

**The real traced runs** (needs keys; produces the before/after + neatlogs evidence):

```bash
cp .env.example .env          # add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and NEATLOGS_API_KEY
python run.py v1              # baseline agent  -> runs/v1.json + neatlogs trace
python run.py v2              # improved agent  -> runs/v2.json + neatlogs trace
python compare.py            # -> docs/BEFORE_AFTER.md
```

See [`docs/SETUP.md`](docs/SETUP.md) for the full walkthrough (including Entire on Windows and the cfo.ai signup).

## Safety / design notes

- Each run operates on an **isolated temp copy** of the repo — the original is never mutated.
- The agent may edit source files and run `pytest` in that sandbox; it cannot touch anything outside it.
- Runs cost real Anthropic tokens. Set `FIXPOINT_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5` for cheap practice runs.

=================== dynaayowilliams-dot__quickhealth README
# QuickHealth

QuickHealth is a hackathon prototype of an AI-assisted clerking and triage interface. It asks one history question at a time, adapts follow-up questions to the answers, and can produce a structured clerking note and plain-language summary. It is **not a diagnostic tool** and does not replace a health professional.

## Who it is for

The prototype is intended for demonstration to nurses, health workers, and hackathon reviewers interested in history-taking workflows in Nigeria. It has general, paediatric, antenatal, and postpartum pathways. Use made-up training cases only. Do not enter real patient information.

## Run it on Windows

Open PowerShell and run these commands from the project folder:

```powershell
Set-Location C:\Users\HP\Documents\quickhealth
py -3 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Create a private `.env` from the placeholder template if you do not already have one, then edit it locally:

```powershell
if (-not (Test-Path .env)) { Copy-Item .env.example .env }
notepad .env
```

Set `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, and `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in that private file. Do not paste or commit those values. `.env` is listed in `.gitignore`; `.env.example` has placeholders only.

Start QuickHealth:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m streamlit run app.py
```

Streamlit prints a local address in the PowerShell window and usually opens it in a browser. Use only fictional cases. The app displays a medical disclaimer and danger-sign emergency notice.

Run the automated tests and scripted evaluation:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -v
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe run_eval.py --version v2 --demo-recovery
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe cost_report.py
```

The SQLite database is stored locally at `data\quickhealth.sqlite3`; the `data` folder is ignored by Git. Do not put real patient data in it.

## Architecture

The app is split into small Python components. In each user turn, safety rules run before the app asks another model question.

1. **Intake and pathway selection** — `quickhealth/intake.py` and `quickhealth/pathways.py` identify the likely patient pathway from the fictional history. The pathway rules cover infants under two months, children under five, pregnancy by trimester (including unknown trimester), postpartum, other adults, and unknown patient type.
2. **Adaptive clerking loop** — `quickhealth/clerking.py` asks for one concise question at a time and uses the prior answers to guide the next question. Pathway guidance adds child, caregiver, pregnancy, or postpartum history topics.
3. **Rules-based red-flag checker** — `quickhealth/safety_rules.py` reads the pathway rules from `rules/red_flags.json`. It alone assigns `EMERGENCY_NOW`, `SEE_CLINICIAN_TODAY`, or `ROUTINE`. An emergency stops routine questioning. Missing or unsafe-to-assess rules must not silently produce a routine outcome.
4. **Completeness check** — `quickhealth/verification.py` checks pathway-required sections before the app can finish. Prescribed, herbal/traditional, and over-the-counter medicine history are separate required sections. Unknown or unanswered items remain incomplete.
5. **Contradiction check** — `quickhealth/verification.py` checks recorded facts and pauses for clarification when it finds a material conflict. Structured checks include age/development and LMP/gestational-age comparisons. Model-assisted free-text detection can suggest a candidate, but does not decide urgency or silently resolve the facts.
6. **Note generator** — `quickhealth/clerking.py` asks the OpenAI model to format the history as a structured note and plain-language summary after the safety and verification gates allow completion. The model does not assign urgency or diagnose.
7. **SQLite state store** — `quickhealth/storage.py` saves session history, verification state, urgency, pathway, and any completed note in SQLite. It also records aggregate model token counts and call latency for the cost report; it does not need those counts to make a safety decision.

The Streamlit UI is in `app.py` and `quickhealth/ui.py`. The application is a prototype: pathway selection and free-text matching can be imperfect, and it needs clinical review before any use beyond fictional demonstrations.

## neatlogs tracing

QuickHealth initializes neatlogs with workflow name `quickhealth-clerking` and OpenAI instrumentation before importing the OpenAI client. The app reads `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` from `.env` and calls `neatlogs.flush()` when the session ends so queued spans can be sent to the Neatlogs workspace configured for that key.

Named spans cover the clerking workflow, intake and pathway selection, adaptive questions, rules-based red-flag checking, completeness and contradiction checks, note generation, SQLite operations, and storage retry recovery. The scripted evaluator tags its traces with the `--version` label and fictional case ID. The failure-recovery demo has a parent workflow span and a `sqlite_write_recovery` span. Its safe attributes report the operation, attempt/retry counts, recovery status, and version; patient answers and keys are not intended as span attributes. App-defined spans disable automatic input/output capture, and a masking function is configured for trace content. Review the Neatlogs workspace access and retention settings for your own deployment.

The SQLite cost metrics are a separate local record of aggregate input tokens, output tokens, and model-call time. `cost_report.py` reads these numbers for completed sessions and calculates estimated average cost using the configured model's standard rates. Earlier sessions without recorded token counts cannot contribute to those averages. This report does not retrieve historical spans from Neatlogs.

## Entire session recording

The repository owner has Entire CLI enabled to record coding-agent work sessions. Entire records development activity; Git commits record repository snapshots. Neither Entire nor Git is the app's runtime session store or the Neatlogs observability system. Keep `.env` and patient data out of both Git commits and shared session materials.

## Scripted evaluation results

The repository's saved fictional-case results show these totals:

| Evaluation | Passed | Failed |
|---|---:|---:|
| v1 (rerun on restored cases) | 14 / 14 | 0 |
| v2 (rerun on restored cases) | 14 / 14 | 0 |

Both reports were rerun against the same restored fictional case definitions. O1 is again a small headache followed by blurred vision in a 28-week pregnancy, with expected `EMERGENCY_NOW`; the rules now conservatively escalate when a headache and visual change are both reported. O4 again describes much less fetal movement at 36 weeks and expects `SEE_CLINICIAN_TODAY`. P1, P6, and O2 retain their original intended expected outcomes. The earlier saved v1/v2 reports used different O1/O4 inputs or expectations and are superseded by these reruns.

The v2 run includes a separate recovery demonstration: it injects one temporary SQLite busy error, retries the fictional write once, and records successful recovery. The saved summary is `results/v2.json`.

## Safety and guideline-source notes

- QuickHealth must not diagnose. If a differential is ever shown, it must be labelled **for clinician consideration**.
- The application is not medical advice. Its visible notice directs people to call emergency services for danger signs.
- Use fictional cases only. Do not enter names, contact details, or any other real patient information.
- Urgency comes from deterministic rules in `rules/red_flags.json`, not from the language model. When the checker cannot safely assess a case, it should escalate rather than imply routine care.
- The JSON rules include `source` and `reviewed_by_clinician` metadata. Every current rule has `reviewed_by_clinician: false`. These rules have not been clinician-reviewed as part of this project; source labels are recorded metadata, not proof that this implementation faithfully applies a guideline.

The source labels in the current rules file refer to:

- WHO, *Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) Chart Booklet*.
- WHO, *Management of the Sick Young Infant Aged Up to 2 Months*.
- WHO, *Recommendations on Postnatal Care of the Mother and Newborn* (2013), postpartum danger signs.
- WHO maternal danger signs and danger signs after childbirth.
- Nigeria Federal Ministry of Health ANC Orientation Package / ANC Orientation Package for Health Care Providers and Safe Motherhood guidance.
- Nigeria Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, *National Guideline for the Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage* (2024).
- Nigeria Federal Ministry of Health postpartum care and Safe Motherhood guidance.

The rule file itself lists the source attached to each rule. The rules and wording still need review by a qualified clinician familiar with current Nigerian guidance before any use with real people.

## Limitations

- This is a hackathon prototype and has **not been clinically validated**. Passing scripted tests does not demonstrate clinical safety, accuracy, or improved outcomes.
- Red-flag recognition uses explicit text patterns and can miss an unexpected phrase or misunderstand context. An answer that is ambiguous or not covered must be checked by a human; the app is not an emergency service.
- The model can ask an incomplete or unsuitable question and can format an inaccurate note. A health professional must review any output.
- Rules are source-labelled but not clinician-reviewed (`reviewed_by_clinician: false`). They may be incomplete, over- or under-inclusive, and may not reflect all current local protocols.
- To meet the O1 fictional case's conservative emergency expectation, the pregnancy headache/visual-change pattern also matches a headache described as small. The named source phrase refers to severe headache with visual changes; this broader matcher requires clinician review and is not represented as a guideline-confirmed threshold.
- The v1/v2 evaluation uses a small set of scripted fictional cases and a scripted model substitute. It is a software behavior check, not a clinical evaluation. Some v1/v2 expected inputs changed as described above.
- The cost report only covers sessions whose model responses included token usage and whose note was completed after usage tracking was added. It uses standard uncached token rates, so actual billing may differ because of caching, model/provider changes, or other fees.
- SQLite is local to this machine and is not a managed clinical record system. Protect the computer and delete fictional test records when they are no longer needed.

## Development checkpoints

Git commits and pushes publish code checkpoints on the repository's `main` branch. Entire recordings are a separate record of the coding-agent work session; they do not replace the code history in Git.

# Hemline

**Hospital coordination, from request to verified handoff.**

Hemline interprets transfer goals and messy staff replies, tracks readiness, recovers from porter rejection and destination delays, and requires receiving-team acknowledgement before completion.

## Run locally

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env.local
npm run dev
# in another terminal
npm run worker:dev
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000. No credentials are required for the **explicit local fixture adapter** and embedded PostgreSQL. That adapter is deterministic, not an LLM. Configure the Aivar gateway with claude-sonnet-4.6 to use the real chat tool loop and neatlogs to export real traces.

Try Bed 18 first. Bed 4 intentionally has a stale reference in another patient's bed history. Manual exploration begins paused. Choose guided playback before confirming a request to activate labelled simulated staff replies. A visitor still confirms the original nurse request and material rescheduling.

## Ward interface

The ward fills the viewport. Patient bays are interactive overlays on the ward scene asset from the user's previous [project](https://github.com/Abhinav-Prabhakar/Warden), reused at the user's request. Hemline keeps its own encounters, state machine, agent tools, database and telemetry. Selecting a bed opens a contextual staff-action panel; history opens from the left rail. The clock menu contains playback, scenario and usage controls. No clinical measurements or medication workflows are imported. Route positions illustrate recorded workflow stages, not tracked staff locations.

The voice dock supports browser dictation with transcript review and optional spoken recorded summaries. Mobile supports horizontal ward exploration and contextual panels; unsupported browsers retain text input. Routes are static; no looping movement implies tracked staff. The attention queue, sync age, readiness evidence and receiving acknowledgement show recorded operational facts. Pickup deadlines are labelled as simulation time and ETA is explicitly unavailable. Live microphone permission and recognition accuracy remain unverified.

## Implementation status

Implemented: web board, role actions, browser dictation with review, durable PostgreSQL aggregate transactions, offers, destination delays, interpretation proposals, guided staff, controllable clock, isolation, quotas, OpenAI-compatible Claude/neatlogs adapters, worker supervision and Render blueprint.

Verified externally: Claude gateway text response, Neatlogs diagnostic export/readback, and live agent activations with finalized workflow/tool traces; 47/48 activation cases passed, and the failed delay case passed 3/3 targeted reruns after a source-ID fix.

Not yet externally verified: hosted Supabase/Render, final 48-case rerun after the prompt fix, cfo.ai business output, and live browser microphone behavior. The full 48-case suite scored 47/48; a source-ID correction subsequently passed three targeted reruns. A complete rerun after that correction remains a release gate.

This is a synthetic hackathon prototype, not a hospital deployment. Do not enter real patient information. Local fixture checks do not establish live agent quality.

## Verification

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run test:integration
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
npm run build
# needs configured real provider
npm run provider:smoke
npm run eval
```

Browser tests require a running development worker. Configure a dedicated test database for hosted integration tests, never the public demo database.

## Development notes

Supplemental specifications, development history and generated trace/test evidence are retained locally and excluded from this published source repository. Only the root README is published as Markdown.

## Hosting

One Render service supervises `next start` and the worker. Supabase supplies hosted PostgreSQL and anonymous authentication. Review `render.yaml` and operations before provisioning. Public creation stays disabled until authentication/CAPTCHA and database access are configured.

MIT license. All seeded patients, staff, and hospital responses are fictional.

Private local demos default to a $1 per-sandbox model allowance (`LOCAL_SANDBOX_MODEL_BUDGET_USD`); public sandboxes retain the $0.25 cap. Both remain subject to the $10 overall model budget. Budget reservations and usage persist across restarts. A transfer paused by a budget refusal can be resumed by switching to Coordinator and selecting Resume coordination after the limit is corrected.

## Interrupted transfer validation

Bed 21 → CT is supported alongside Bed 18 → Radiology. A nurse interruption pauses dispatch and produces a replacement proposal. Nurse confirmation cancels the old transfer and creates a new draft with independent readiness. An accepted assignment requires porter cancellation acknowledgement first; collected patients require staff intervention. Late acceptance is rejected, audited and shown in the simulated porter inbox. Deterministic collection/arrival/handoff actions do not consume additional model activations.

Run `npx tsx scripts/test-interrupted-transfer.ts` with provider and neatlogs credentials to reproduce the isolated in-memory PostgreSQL test. It uses real model calls and trace export; staff confirmations are explicitly scripted. On 2026-10-10 the complete scenario passed with Claude Sonnet 4.6, five activations, estimated cost $0.2202123, trace `b1826c145f143a7d0f4667bdf52a5332`. Authenticated neatlogs readback succeeded. Local evidence is ignored by Git. The preserved baseline showed the old guard already rejected stale acceptance; missing replacement support and rejection audit were the improvements. This targeted run does not establish the 48-case release gate or deployed restart verification.

Prompt v5 compacts model context and records tool arguments. The latest isolated interruption rerun passed at estimated $0.1779987 with trace `065487d6cb5a4d635721a4e487fc6bf7`. 53 deterministic/integration checks passed after the fixes. Broader guided browser findings and preserved failures are recorded in docs/testing.md; a targeted pass does not imply the release suite is complete.

Final local validation (2026-10-11): prompt v6 interrupted-transfer scenario passed with authenticated neatlogs export; 55 domain/integration tests and the full six-test browser suite passed, alongside typecheck, lint and build. Guided rejection recovery and receiving delay both passed with the live provider. Evidence: `evidence/interruption-validation.md` (local, ignored by Git). Public provisioning and the 48-case release evaluation remain pending; latest private guided usage exceeds the public $0.25 cap.

### Verified stale-acceptance HTTP scenario

`npx tsx scripts/test-stale-http.ts` first verifies localhost is development with local embedded PostgreSQL and real provider/tracing configured, then resets only the named synthetic test ward. It preserves other wards and global spending. The reset endpoint is disabled for production, public provisioning, and hosted databases. The script exercises authenticated HTTP requests, waits for the real worker/LLM, and saves assertions to `evidence/stale-http-result.json`.

Watch `/test/live` in the local browser while it runs. This read-only development view shows test aliases T-001/T-002, actual UUIDs, statuses and events. Samir's delayed acceptance was rejected after cancellation; Leena's replacement completed only after receiving-team handoff. `COMPLETED` is the domain's handoff-complete status. The labelled stale-availability fixture keeps Samir unavailable for the replacement. Staff and patient data remain synthetic; API, persistence, model and telemetry calls are real.

### Deploy through Vercel GitHub import

Import this GitHub repository as a Next.js project, root directory `.`. `vercel.json` selects `npm ci` and `npm run build:web`; Node 22 is selected by `package.json`. The authenticated internal worker endpoint has a 180-second function limit. Its PostgreSQL migration is explicitly included in the serverless function bundle. Vercel runs the web/API application. A separate always-running worker calls the authenticated tick endpoint; Vercel does not run `npm start` or the continuous supervisor. Set `REMOTE_WORKER=true` on the worker. If deployment protection is enabled, its automation bypass secret goes only on the worker. The worker does not need database, LLM or neatlogs keys. The original single-service Render deployment remains available in `render.yaml`.

Vercel server environment: `DATABASE_URL` (dedicated hosted PostgreSQL / Supabase session pooler), `SESSION_SECRET`, `WORKER_SECRET`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, `MODEL_API`, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`, model pricing ceilings and existing spending limits. For public provisioning, also set Supabase URL/anon key, Turnstile site key/secret, `APP_BASE_URL` and `PUBLIC_DEMO_ENABLED=true`; enable anonymous auth and register the production hostname with Turnstile. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values must be configured before the build. Keep public provisioning disabled until these are verified. Local embedded PostgreSQL and development test/reset routes are unavailable in production.

Start with an isolated hosted test database and provisioning disabled; then verify DB health, worker heartbeat, real provider/tracing and owned synthetic test flows before enabling public access. A deployed page alone does not establish agent readiness. =================== Rahmat9009__lc-rescue-desk README
# LC Rescue Desk

A neatHack prototype for investigating LC document conflicts, proposing issuer corrections, recording human approval, responding to simulated counterparty replies, and checking revised document versions.

## Current working scope

- English UTF-8 text-native LC, invoice and bill of lading, up to 16,000 characters each.
- Source-grounded extraction, currency/reference/explicit consignee conflicts, numeric/date checks and calculated presentation deadline.
- Exporter correction and carrier reissue request drafts. Approval binds source versions.
- Revised versions and originals retained; independent recheck; complete JSON audit export.
- Carrier delay and buyer-waiver scenarios produce safe escalation.
- Owner-scoped D1 persistence with compare-and-swap revision checks.

**Demo mode is deterministic fixture execution. It runs zero LLM agents.** Live mode executes three document investigators concurrently, then a remedy planner and counterparty coordinator. Code, rather than the model, controls validation, approval and final state. Full live workflow execution and persisted trace readback remain unverified.

No bank-ready certification is claimed. Full UCP/ISBP interpretation, bank holidays, original-document authenticity, PDFs/OCR, recipient verification, external messaging and bank submission are outside this build. Only explicit consignee terms are compared; general name variation is not implemented. Counterparty reply scenarios are simulated in both modes. Live revised documents are user uploads, not model-generated third-party instruments.

## Local development

Use Node 24 and pnpm. From this folder:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build
pnpm exec wrangler d1 execute DB --local --config dist/server/wrangler.json --persist-to .wrangler/state --file drizzle/0000_steady_namorita.sql
pnpm run dev
```

Apply that schema only to a fresh local database. Production uses tracked schema migrations automatically. For repeated development, preserve the local database. The Vite dev server uses a local auth mock and serves the demo at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`; the built Wrangler server started by `pnpm run start` requires Sites-authenticated identity and does not provide a local sign-in route.

For live local runs, keep an ignored root `.dev.vars` with the names in `.env.example`. The Vite dev server reads this root file. Every build copies it into `dist/server/.dev.vars` for the generated Wrangler config, and `pnpm run start` refreshes that copy before launch. Keep the root file and local `.wrangler/state` database; rebuilds do not require another schema import. Do not commit either secret file. For a hosted run, configure the same values as server runtime settings, not in client code.

```sh
pnpm run typecheck
node --test tests/domain.test.mjs
# Requires the built Worker from pnpm run build:
node --test tests/api.test.mjs
node --test tests/live.test.mjs
```

The in-process API test runs Miniflare with an isolated test D1 database. It does not open a preview server. Browser visual/interaction QA has not been performed in this environment.

## Entire development history

Entire tracks this project through approved Codex CLI hooks. On this Windows machine, launch Codex with:

```sh
codex -c windows.sandbox=mxc
```

Imported checkpoints represent earlier sessions. New captured work can be linked to Git commits.

## Live model and neatlogs configuration

- `GEMINI_API_KEY`: server secret for Google's Gemini API.
- `LC_MODEL`: a Gemini model ID available to that key and supporting JSON output. The verified local choice is `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`; keep the selected value in `.dev.vars`.
- `NEATLOGS_WRITE_KEY`: server secret, **HTTP write key** starting `nlw_`.
- `NEATLOGS_PROJECT`: exact neatlogs project **name** (not its UUID).

The SDK project key is a different credential. This hosted Worker uses the documented HTTP integration because the Node SDK requires dynamic code generation unavailable in Workers.

Live document input and model outputs are sent to Gemini. The Worker uses raw `fetch` to Google's [OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai) with JSON-object output, minimal reasoning and an 8,192-token output budget. Start with synthetic or anonymized documents. Failed live actions preserve the previous case state and record the failure; they do not fall back to fixtures. Provider-reported token usage is accumulated. No pricing or currency cost is invented; use the selected model's actual billing for cfo.ai.

A small direct request with `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` returned HTTP 200 and parseable JSON with provider usage. That verifies local authentication and this response format only; full live investigations and neatlogs readback still need separate verification.

Tracing builds one complete nested WORKFLOW/AGENT/LLM/GUARDRAIL tree per invocation and posts it to `https://ingest.neatlogs.com/v1/trace` with `User-Agent: LCRescueDesk/0.1`. Every node ends before export; all concurrent workers are awaited even when one fails. Status, timing, model IDs, provider-reported tokens, extraction quotes and deterministic findings remain in the trace. The service-generated trace ID and acknowledged span count are recorded only on a valid receipt. Tokens are absent when usage is unknown, rather than invented as zero.

The HTTP trace intentionally omits raw source documents, exact system prompts, duplicate AGENT input/output copies, repeated finding details in planner/coordinator inputs, and full coordinator draft text. Document kind, version and byte length identify the saved source; LLM outputs retain extraction quotes, and the guardrail retains the checked findings. Originals and full drafts remain in the local case. This limits duplicated telemetry while preserving the full span tree. Transport diagnostics showed a 6,144-byte single-node trace and a 6,000-byte 12-node synthetic trace accepted, while 8,192- and 12,288-byte traces received HTML 403 responses from `awselb/2.0`. The exact upstream limit is unconfirmed; larger valid traces can still be rejected. Failure events record request bytes and node counts without changing the case result. Neatlogs payload readback remains unverified.

The Node SDK local Doctor initially passed, but the mocked live Worker test exposed an EvalError while importing it. The hosted application was changed to HTTP injection; the SDK diagnostic does not validate this hosted HTTP path.

### Required evidence loop

1. Configure the HTTP write key, exact project name and model settings securely.
2. Open a **live** case with synthetic source documents and run investigation.
3. Find the exact trace ID in the audit trail and read it back in the neatlogs dashboard.
4. Check a finalized root, three parallel investigator agents and their LLM children, deterministic guardrail, remedy planner and coordinator; inspect source/output and provider usage.
5. Exercise an invalid JSON or unsupported extraction branch; inspect the real failure trace, fix the cause, and rerun with a fresh correlation marker.
6. Inspect recheck and simulated-reply workflows separately. Record actual trace links in Evidence.

| Workflow | Trigger | Expected capture | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Investigation | Investigate live case | Root; 3 investigators/LLMs; guardrail; planner/LLM; coordinator/LLM for supported conflicts | Pending actual application run + finalized readback |
| Recheck | Upload revised documents, then recheck | New root; 3 investigators/LLMs; guardrail; correction roles only if new findings | Pending |
| Reply assessment | Simulated delay/waiver or uploaded revision receipt in live case | Root; coordinator/LLM | Pending |
| Fixture rehearsal | Demo actions | No neatlogs export or LLM calls | API and domain tests |

An export request, a local Doctor pass, or a trace ID alone is not evidence that the application's trace was persisted correctly.

## Sponsor setup still required

- [neatlogs setup guide](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/neatlogs-setup-guide.html): create organization/project and collect the HTTP write key (`nlw_`) and exact project name for this Worker. The SDK guide also describes a separate Project API key. Never paste keys into chat.
- [Entire event guide](https://hack.entire.io/neathacks-2026/): connect the **GitHub development repository**, install the official CLI and create an accessible checkpoint. The Sites source commit is not an Entire checkpoint. This guide returned HTTP 403 during research; no CLI commands are invented here.
- [cfo.ai event signup](https://cfo.ai/neathacks): the organizer's supplied email says signup requires a card and to cancel immediately under Settings → Billing. Create the actual plan and attach its link.
- [Discord support](https://neatlogs.com/discord): ask organizers about credits or account setup issues.

## Demo rehearsal

1. New case → Synthetic demo → Investigate.
2. Show EUR vs USD and explicit B/L consignee conflict, each with source quotes.
3. Review drafts → Approve correction requests.
4. Receive synthetic revised versions → Recheck. Show retained originals in Documents.
5. Open a second case and choose Carrier delay. Show that the deadline prevents a resolved outcome.
6. Export case evidence, then show **real** sponsor artifacts after account setup.

Do not pitch fixture execution as actual multi-agent execution. No benchmark against a competent single-agent baseline has yet been run. Record fairness, latency, token cost, discrepancy precision and correction outcome when building that comparison.

## Verified build checkpoint

2026-10-10: strict TypeScript check, production build, and all 22 tests passed. Live-runtime tests use mocked model and ingest HTTP endpoints; they do not prove real model quality or neatlogs persistence. Browser interaction and visual QA remain unverified.

### Farid CFO_PLAN
# Autopsy — Business Plan (built with cfo.ai)

> Modeled in the cfo.ai neatHack workspace:
> https://cfo.ai/s/gWOEX-_KzKXUshRa
> The headline below is what the model found — including the part that
> hurts. We keep it honest: the fix is the plan, not the spin.

## What we sell

**Autopsy** is a root-cause debugger for production AI agents. Observability
tools show *what* went wrong; Autopsy tells you *why* — by joining runtime
traces with development history (which coding-agent session/commit
introduced the regression) and returning a diagnosis with verifiable
evidence plus a suggested fix.

**Buyer:** platform / AI-infra teams shipping LLM agents to production.
**Pain:** a failed agent run costs an engineer 30–90 min of manual trace
reading + `git blame` archaeology. Autopsy compresses that to ~2 min.

## Pricing

| Tier | Price | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 25–50 diagnoses/mo, 1 repo |
| Pro | $79/mo/seat | 500 diagnoses/mo |
| Team | $499/mo (5 seats) | 2k diagnoses/mo, CI gate, SSO |
| Enterprise | ~$4k/mo (placeholder) | 15k diagnoses, self-hosted, SLA |

Overage: $0.50 per diagnosis — required, not optional (see below).

## What the model found (the honest part)

Variable cost per diagnosis ≈ **$0.35** (LLM $0.30 — 86% of cost — +
observability $0.02 + infra $0.03). At 40% utilization:

| Plan | Revenue | Cost to serve | Gross margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pro (2 seats) | $158 | $140 | 11% |
| Team | $499 | $700 | **−40%** |
| Enterprise | $4,000 | $2,100 | 48% |

At list prices **Team loses ~$201/customer/month**; blended margin at
month 12 is −3% to −10% and the business never breaks even — $500k runs
out in ~21 months in every scenario.

## The fix (margin scenario)

1. **Cost curve:** $0.35 → **$0.17**/diagnosis — cache repeated
   investigations, route simpler failures to smaller models, batch calls.
2. **Reprice:** Team $499 → **$799** with overage charge; trim included
   allotments (Team 5k→2k, Free 50→25); Enterprise = cost-plus.
3. **Hard caps / overage** so heavy users can't sink the margin.

Result: blended gross margin → **~64%**, cash-flow positive **month 16**
(Jan 2028), cash bottoms at ~$323k

## Project

**Autopsy** — a debugger for AI-agent mistakes. It investigates a failed
agent run by joining the runtime timeline (neatlogs trace) with the
development timeline (Entire checkpoints + transcripts) and produces an
evidence-backed diagnosis: root cause, failing step, culprit commit/session,
suggested fix.

**Team:** Last Commit
**Repo:** https://github.com/FaridMahmudlu/neathack-agent

## Use of Entire

All product code changes were made through OpenCode agent sessions captured
by Entire. Three checkpoints on `main`:

| Checkpoint ID | Commit | What it is |

| `01M4K1KECVQ0VNT4GVGB9KCB90` | `f4df4da09ea6797b4d499e1d1837fbc1ad940129` | OpenCode setup + project notes |
| `01M4K1P5A9NYJJNRY2D9XKJ08P` | `dece4846baaed3c5961447af4c0d99a7dd273ed1` | The regression (debug flip committed) |

| `01M4K6CBKM821B6WC4YCNWE81Z` | `4663486` | **Autopsy's own fix** — diagnosed, applied via OpenCode, verified, + regression test |
| `01M4K6VBSVW7RCAN0WJDGGNBHF` | `836eb38` | Scenario 2 culprit — prompt relaxed, agent stopped calling tools |
| `01M4K77FZR530VRPBX8CTB56VM` | `eab70ea` | Scenario 2 fix — strict corpus-only prompt restored |

1. **Code regression** (`dece484`): sort flipped → wrong retrieval →
   incomplete answer. Autopsy named the checkpoint and the `reverse=False`
   line. → `demo_assets/diagnosis_bugged_run.json`
2. **Prompt regression** (`836eb38`): corpus-only constraint relaxed →
